tips.text: After a snow of 2 inches or more, Bend Park and Rec clears its rec centers and parking lots first, then works through trails like the Pine Nursery Park loop and the Drake Park paths.
The Pine Nursery Trail is a good winter stroller loop: it is fairly level, east Bend tends to get less snow, and park crews regularly clear it.
Skyline Sports Complex is the one Bend park groomed for cross-country skiing, by XC Oregon volunteers. Keep boots, sleds and dogs off the groomed tracks.
Cross-country skiing and snowshoeing are allowed in every Bend park, so a snowy neighborhood park can be a first snowshoe outing.
Shevlin Park and Riley Ranch close at dusk, and in heavy snow the Riley Ranch lot may not be cleared, so plan winter visits early in the day.
At Juniper rec swim, kids under 10 need a supervising person 16 or older, and the small pool is saved for kids 6 and under or non-swimmers.
The Pavilion switches surfaces with the seasons: ice from late October to early April, roller skating from mid-April through September.
SHARC's indoor pool in Sunriver is open year-round and kept warm, with tot bubblers and a zero-entry shallow end for little ones.
Prineville's Kiwanis Splash Park in Stryker Park runs June through September, a good cool-off on hot afternoons.
On smoky days, Redmond's park district tones down outdoor programs once the air quality index passes 100, since kids are more sensitive to smoke. It is a good cue to move play indoors.
The Circuit in Bend asks for youth reservations on weekends and school break days, so book ahead before a no-school day.
Bring a small towel after rain or frost to dry off slides and swing seats before the kids climb on.
On hot afternoons, touch metal slides and dark surfaces first; shaded play structures and morning visits stay cooler.
For snow play, pack a spare pair of dry socks and mittens for the car ride home.

challenges.text: Visit any playground with snow on the ground and stamp it in your family passport.

challenges.title: Three towns
